description.value: A randomized, placebo-controlled pharmaco-fMRI study assessing the effects of individually titrated high-dose baclofen on alcohol cue reactivity and functional connectivity in alcohol-dependent patients, compared with healthy controls and placebo treatment.

spans.text: For the first time, we assessed the effects of individually titrated high-dose baclofen on cue reactivity and functional connectivity in alcohol-dependent (AD) patients in a randomized controlled trial (RCT).

description.value: A 2-arm, parallel-group, double-blind, randomized and placebo-controlled design with baseline and second scanning sessions.

spans.text: Cue reactivity paradigm

description.value: Participants viewed blocks of alcoholic and non-alcoholic beverage pictures during fMRI, with craving ratings between blocks.

instructions.value: Rate current craving for alcohol between stimulation blocks by moving a cursor using left and right button presses.

stimuli.value: Pictures of alcoholic and non-alcoholic beverages; two picture sets were used at t1 and t2.
